knowledge_graph.title: Epidemiology of HIV/AIDS
knowledge_graph.description: The global pandemic of HIV/AIDS began in 1981, and is an ongoing worldwide public health issue. According to the World Health Organization, by 2023, HIV/AIDS had killed approximately 40.4 million people, and approximately 39 million people were infected with HIV globally.

text_blocks.snippet: The AIDS crisis, stemming from the HIV epidemic, has been a global health challenge since the early 1980s, with significant impact on individuals, communities, and healthcare systems worldwide. While significant progress has been made in treatment and prevention, HIV/AIDS remains a major public health concern.

text_blocks.snippet: Key Aspects of the AIDS Crisis:

list.title: Emergence and Early Impact:
list.snippet: The first cases of what would later be identified as AIDS were reported in the early 1980s, initially affecting primarily gay men. The disease was characterized by a range of opportunistic infections and cancers due to a weakened immune system.

list.title: HIV Transmission and Progression:
list.snippet: HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, is primarily transmitted through sexual contact, sharing needles, and from mother to child during pregnancy, delivery, or breastfeeding. Without treatment, HIV can progress to AIDS, a stage where the immune system is severely damaged, making individuals vulnerable to life-threatening illnesses.
